subject: Inference of population size (and trend) in species that are rare and hard to detect

messages.author: 074a030d0cd7e490
messages.subject: Inference of population size (and trend) in species that are rare and hard to detect
parts:
Dear colleagues,

For once, a non-statistical modeling question that hopefully may be of relevance to this group. Student Paula Ledezma and myself used N-mixture models to estimate a 8-year time series of Resplendent Quetzal abundance based on unmarked individual point counts in the Monteverde Cloud Forest Preserve of Costa Rica. We also used the data to infer a population trend, based on the estimation of an effect of time on abundance. The greatest challenge of this work is the low detection probability of Quetzals, who seem to move about substantially between replicate point counts, combined with their low density.

In the manuscript's introduction, we would like to contextualize our study among other attempts to infer temporal trends based on counts of unmarked individuals that are either difficult to detect or just move about too much for the assumption of closure between replicate counts. There seem to be few examples of this or we are not looking in the right places.

Any thoughts or reading suggestions will be very welcome.

Thank you,

Gonçalo Ferraz
